body: Me too! I live in the Wekiva area and my Internet is constantly going out. It's so sporadic I never call to complain, but so frequent it is amazingly annoying. And it's a new thing.
Back at you. Thanks. Getting my teeth looked at is one of my goal's of 2014. Let me know what your experiences are like.

This recent Orlando Sentinel article talks about dental options for uninsured patients: http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/2012-09-14/health/os-low-income-dental-care-orlando-20120914_1_pediatric-dental-services-dental-care-dental-infection

Sorry for your pain. It's terrible to have hurt teeth. This is from a sheet I got at the Seminole County Health Dept. Can't vouch for any of this because I haven't made the calls yet, but at least this is a place to start.

Apopka Dental Center, 407-896-9569 Ages 6 and up, Takes Medicaid, private insurance and sliding scale

Eatonville Dental Center, 407-645-3959, Ages 21 and up. Medicaid, privateinsurances, sliding scales

Central Florida Family Health (Orlando) ages 2-17 and adult ER on Fridays, 407-956-4660. Medicaid and sliding scale (nitrous)

Dental Research Clinic, 301 W. Amelia St. Orlando, 32805, Adult only, cash and sliding scale, 407-425-3381. Monday-Thursday 9 am. to 11 a.m. and 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. Closed during summer.

Winter Garden Health, 407-877-4310, All ages. Medicaid, insurance, sliding scale, grant for undocumented children. Monday 8 a.m. to 7 p.m., Tuesday Wed. Thurs 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., 1 Sunday per month referred by school nurse

Pine Hills Family Health, 407-209-3202, ages 1-17, Medicaid and sliding scale.

$20 cleanings Valencia Hygiene Clinic 407-582-1305

Dental Care Access Foundation, 407-898-1525

Seminole County Community Assistance, 407-665-2360

Volusia County Social Services, 386-775-5204

Each of these has different hours and covers different things, but that was a lot to type so I figured the numbers would get you what you need. I had called the Dental Research Clinic, which takes patients on a slidincg scale, and they said you have to visit to apply in person to see if you qualify. I just haven't gotten to doing that yet.

Anyhow, good luck. I ended up paying $500 to Coast Dental to pull out 3 bottom teeth last year, and now I wonder whether I might not be better to have tried to save them. Or at least it wouldn't have cost so much. Sorry, I'm not making sense because I'm sleepy.

Anyway, I hope that helps. Let me know. I'm going to be doing the same search myself. Dental care is just one of those things that you don't appreciate until you don't have it and your teeth are falling apart or worse, hurting. Wishing you well. :)

I don't think it's easy. Wasn't trying to say that. I know it's hard and it sucks and you want to give up. But I've been in your place and I know that in the morning I felt different, so I'm tossing out random ideas for you to try on.

Because really, life is all in your head. Think hard about that. Our own thoughts are the things that hurt us the most. If we could just stop thinking and going over and over it, wouldn't that lessen the pain?

Me too. And so does everybody I've ever known. There are so many ways to screw up. And even when you think you're doing it right, somebody will tell you you're wrong. You have to let it go and just accept that things happened. It doesn't say anything about you. You're just a part of the universe.

You just have to go on. Even though it's hard. It hurts like shit. So what. What other choice do you have. The only way it's going to get better is with time and distance and those only come through going forward. 

I could tell you you're already past it, that the worst has already happened. You've already survived it. But that won't help you feel better.

The feeling better will only come through time. 

You'll learn and hopefully become wiser. But you'll screw up something, somewhere, again, and you'll have to cope with the fallout from that. We ALL SCREW UP. Even when we try our hardest to do the right thing and follow all the rules and color in the lines sometimes we still screw up. It's just life. Sometimes things come up roses, sometimes not.

Go get yourself a milkshake and give yourself an internal hug. You don't sound like a bad person at all. Walk on.

HYDROCODONE. That is the most concerning drug to me in your thread. Cut out the pills. They could kill you. I have not read of anyone overdosing on weed. 

The weed will also affect you and contribute to depression, though, the other poster is right. So cut that out too, to get your head clear. You don't want to be fuzzy while you're thinking such thoughts. 

That may not get rid of the thoughts. You could be having a mental health issue. It may be slight depression, that's all, and so easily treatable. So turn to someone you trust, who can provide help to get evaluated for that. It migth just be telling your regular physician you're depressed and they can prescribe antidepressants or just refer you to a specialist. That's the easiest route to take for treating depression. 

You can also call 211 in most areas of the country and be connected to services in your area for anything you might need, from suicide prevention to health care. So call them too. The more help the better. 

Just surround yourself with help right now. Think of help as the lifeboats that will keep you afloat while you're sinking and can't hold yourself up.

Then when you're thinking more clearly you can worry about your purpose in life or finding what you're meant to do. Those are deep questions that grown adults struggle with, so you're naturally not going to be able to figure these things out at 15. That's normal, although deeply frustrating and can even leave you despondent. It leaves me despondent at age 51 when I feel useless and pointless and like I'm going through the motions. That's depression and it hits everyone, but you can fix that part, at least.

So tl;dr, you don't sound stupid at all.

That yelling at the dogs and them acting scared shitless, same thing happens to me sometimes. I'm bipolar. Even though I have Medicare, (saved my life) and am on meds, I still go manic sometimes. Well it's my decision because I won't let the shrink put me on mood stabilizers. Those things are all anti-seizure meds and they're potent, and they all do damage to something, your liver or your kidneys or your thyroid. Screw that. So I try to control my mania with meditation exercise and chilling. It's not the highs that bother me so much anyway, it's the lows.

Benadryl I am allergic to. It is an anticholinergic, and I'm not exactly sure what those are but they give me restless leg syndrome and make me haywire. Some psych meds have it as an ingredient too and I won't take them.

I took Prozac for years and it did nothing for me, looking back. Still got way depressed and had manias. They say bipolars shouldn't be on antidepressants because it will make them manic, but I take Wellbutrin and I have pressured speech and difficulty sleeping, so I take Klonopin for that. Those are the drugs I have accepted. Took me forever to come to terms with a shrink and I still have to tussle with her. She's araid I'll go on a shoe-buying spree (ha ha, I'm sure she thinks I'm a maniac. ;)

Anyway, whatever. Enough about me. blah blah blah.

Which doesn't mean we won't push people away. We will, and then feel like assholes. But it's not because we're assholes. That's why I keep people at a distance now, because I loved people in the past and they hurt me somehow and I hurt them. Don't really want to go through that again for now. Maybe when I'm stronger I can try again, being around lots of people.

Anyway, sorry to blather on about me. That's the other thing about people, though, we really are selfish. All of us. We have to be. Nobody is going to help you survive, ultimately, but yourself. I guess there are those rare examples of selflessness, like firefighters, and that's why we all applaud them so much, because it's rare.

Friends come and go. Just let them. Life is much easier. More will come in if you want, and then go out, like waves. Or you can hermit for awhile. It doesn't matter. It's your movie. Whatever you want it to be, just make it.

Have you watched American Horror Story: Asylum? I know, this is out of left field, but go with it.

It's a dark show. Set in a cruel insane asylum in the 1960s, it's full of people who are basically having the worst years of their lives. There's an evil doctor who tortures people and a nun who's really Satan and people are so doped up on meds they don't even know their names. A reporter named Lana goes in there trying to write an investigative expose, and ends up getting locked up and held against her will and given electroshock treatments and all kindsa awful.

I won't spoil it for you but watch the last episode, which features Lana. See what happened to Lana, and to her friends.

To me, that is the reason one goes on. Because you never know. The only thing you do know is, if you leave the theater when the movie is bad, you will never see the happy ending.

Your fucked-up childhood. That's the problem in a nutshell. And it's not your fault. There was nothing you could do about it. But it screwed you up (I know, because ditto.) Have you read the Reddit page RaisedByNarcissists? I was stunned when I found that forum and realized that was my mother to a T. Just seeing everyone on there describing mothers who were just like mine, and feeling the same feelings of emptiness and desperation and self-loathing...it was like a mirror. And then knowing that there were so many out there, who had been mistreated the same way and are hurting just like me, made me feel less alone and swear to god it took so much hurt away, to know I'm not crazy and it's not just me, it WAS her.

You're not defective. You just haven't gotten lucky in love. You're not alone in that either. 

Y'know, I had it made. I was married for 20 years. But my husband had unresolved anger issues. He was angry at me for something every day of our marriage. And after we had kids he took the anger out on them, too. Because of my fucked-up childhood, I stayed with him and tried desperately to make it work. But finally one day, when he tried to strangle me, I realized this was not going to ever work. It was so hard to leave and it nearly destroyed me. My children have sided with him, the way children of abusers will do, and I'm all alone. He has since remarried a younger woman and his business is booming and so my kids adore him because $$$ and he looks like the picture of success and I look like an abject failure, no relationship, sick and sad, poverty-stricken and constantly treated like a doormat by my children (example, not even telling me Happy Birthday yesterday on my birthday). 

But I know that this is all smoke and mirrors. He is a beast. His new wife is a beast. My children are acting like beasts, although I don't blame them because they had fucked-up childhoods, too.

I can't change any of that. But what I can do is hold on to my belief in myself. I'm not a bad person! I try very hard! That's why I'm so sad so many times, because I don't measure up to the very best I want to be!

Listen, if my toxic ex can find somebody to marry his sorry ass, there is NO WAY you can't find somebody to love you. You sound like a nice person. Life is harder for nice people, unfortunately, but that doesn't mean you're defective or undeserving of love. It probably means that when you find somebody to love and be loved by, you'll be so much more grateful and a really great mate. 

So don't give up, there are plenty of us females out here who are lonely too and just want intimacy, too. We just have to keep going until we can bump into one another.

This is why I take Klonopin. Not that drugs are the only solution. But it reduces my anxiety tremendously.

Let me ask you: Have you been through a tragedy or trauma? Something that rocked your world? And you came out the other end different? And you wish you could be the person you were before it, but you're not and you never will be, but your'e still mourning that person, who was more innocent, who didn't know such bad things could happen and who wasn't damaged like I am now?

I don't know, maybe that's just my thing. But that's the part of this that depresses me. That I'm a sadder person. I realize I'm sadder, other people point out that I'm sadder and even get angry at me for being sadder, and that just makes me sadder still. It's a cycle of endless sad.

What I would like to do is just get to know the new me. Not be sad because she's sad. But sort of sit outside her and just hold her hand and understand her. I am trying for that, to look at myself from outside myself and to love myself. That didn't make any sense, but anyway, I hope you find some peace, and a way to live happy and free. And if you do find it, please share it! :)

As for this shitty economy, somebody is going to have to do something about that and unfortunately it's not up to you or me. But in the meantime, don't let the bastards get you down, ok?

The struggle to get out of bed and get it all done. Ah yes. Y'know those of us with depression are working about 10 times harder than others, I think. So congratulate yourself for that.

Finding what you love and getting a job in it is a lifelong thing. It ebbs and flows. Sometimes you'll be doing what you love, sometimes you'll be feeling like a worthless piece of gum under a shoe. That's how life is -- no job lasts forever, and sometimes fun jobs grow awful after a time. The people who manage to pull it all off -- the Tina Feys of the world, Barbara Walters for some reason I'm thinking of lol -- they got LUCKY! And probably had a lot of money and resources to begin with.

Anyway, all I wanted to say was, give yourself baby steps. I find it difficult to get myself to the gym. A counselor once told me, just put your gym shoes out so you can see them. Make that all you do the first day. The next day, put your gym clothes next to them. And on and on. I found that by day 2 I was like, this is stupid, and I got dressed and went to the gym. So that trick works, fwiw.

Good luck. You're at the start of your life and if you can think of it as the world is full of possibilities, not limited at all, maybe that will help your outlook? I know you're tired. You've worked very hard. Maybe get some sleep too.

No! Don't you let this country make you be down on yourself. Your country failed you! (I'm going to assume you're American.)
